subject.title: [RFC] Agent Teleconference — minimum-viable scoped meeting primitive with working prototype

question: Should OpenClaw accept a first-party `meet` lifecycle primitive for agent teleconferences, and what storage/auth/transcript boundary should the MVP use?
rationale: Current main lacks the requested lifecycle, but implementing it adds core CLI, persistent session state, transcript privacy, and cross-agent authorization behavior that cannot be selected safely by automation.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow core MVP
options.body: Define `meet dial/pickup/send/wrap/list/show/transcript` above the existing agent-delivery primitives, use canonical SQLite-backed state or an explicitly named transcript artifact, and require security/state-transition tests.

options.title: Route to plugin until an API gap is proven
options.body: Keep core lean by letting the fork or a plugin carry the workflow unless it identifies a specific missing plugin/runtime API that core should expose.

options.title: Pause for a handoff contract first
options.body: Settle the lower-level handoff id, ack, and delivery ledger semantics before accepting the higher-level meeting lifecycle.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrow core MVP
recommendation.body: Define `meet dial/pickup/send/wrap/list/show/transcript` above the existing agent-delivery primitives, use canonical SQLite-backed state or an explicitly named transcript artifact, and require security/state-transition tests.
